title: Meridian document
description: A Meridian document: an Infrastructure or a ResourceSet. Generated by `meridian schema`; do not edit.

apiVersion.description: The version of the document language this document is written in.

oneOf.description: The first version of the Meridian document language.

kind.description: What the document describes: `Infrastructure` provisions things, `ResourceSet` configures something that exists.

oneOf.description: Provisions things that later documents are applied to: machines, networks, clusters. Compiles for an infrastructure-as-code target and may declare outputs.
Describes the desired state of something that already exists: the packages, files and services on a host, or the workloads on a cluster.

name.description: The document's name. It must be unique among documents of the same kind in a workflow, and it is what `targetHost.ref` refers to.

labels.description: Names and values used to select documents with `-l/--selector`, as in `tier=web,env!=prod`. Labels are not passed to the target.

SecretSource.description: Another place a secret is looked for, when the places before it have nothing.

from.description: The provider the value is fetched from.

oneOf.description: The output of a program, given by `command`. No shell reads it.
A key in the Linux kernel keyring, found by its description, `key`.
A credential systemd passed to this unit, named by `key`.
An item in the freedesktop Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet), found by its `attributes`.
A generic password in the macOS keychain, found by `service` and `account`.

key.description: With `from: env`: the environment variable that holds the value. With `from: keyring`: the description of the key. With `from: systemd-creds`: the name of the credential.

path.description: With `from: file`: the file that holds the value.

command.description: With `from: exec`: the program and its arguments, as a list. No shell reads them.

service.description: With `from: keychain`: the service of the keychain item.

account.description: With `from: keychain`: the account of the keychain item.

attributes.description: With `from: secret-service`: the attributes the item is found by. They are not secret.

allowWideMode.description: With `from: file`: read the file even though others can read it as well.

keepTrailingNewline.description: With `from: file` and `from: systemd-creds`: keep the value's last line ending.

Secret.description: A secret's name and where it comes from. Its value is never written in a document.

name.description: The name the secret is read by, as `secret.<name>`.

from.description: The provider the value is fetched from.

oneOf.description: The output of a program, given by `command`. No shell reads it.
A key in the Linux kernel keyring, found by its description, `key`.
A credential systemd passed to this unit, named by `key`.
An item in the freedesktop Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet), found by its `attributes`.
A generic password in the macOS keychain, found by `service` and `account`.

key.description: With `from: env`: the environment variable that holds the value. With `from: keyring`: the description of the key. With `from: systemd-creds`: the name of the credential.

path.description: With `from: file`: the file that holds the value.

command.description: With `from: exec`: the program and its arguments, as a list. No shell reads them.

service.description: With `from: keychain`: the service of the keychain item.

account.description: With `from: keychain`: the account of the keychain item.

attributes.description: With `from: secret-service`: the attributes the item is found by. They are not secret.

allowWideMode.description: With `from: file`: read the file even though others can read it as well.

keepTrailingNewline.description: With `from: file` and `from: systemd-creds`: keep the value's last line ending.

optional.description: A secret that cannot be found is `null` instead of an error.

fallback.description: The places to look next, in order, when the first has nothing or cannot be used on this machine.

Credential.description: An identity, by name and type: how to prove who you are to a host, a tool or a service. A field that holds secret material reads a declared secret, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`; a value written there is refused.

name.description: The name the credential is used by, such as in `targetHost.credential`.

type.description: What kind of identity it is. The type fixes which fields it takes.

oneOf.description: An AWS identity: `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey`, or a `profile`, or a `roleArn`, with a `region`.
An Azure identity: `tenantId` and `clientId` with a `clientSecret` or a `certificate`, or `managedIdentity: true`, with a `subscriptionId`.
A certificate and its private key, for mutual TLS, with the `ca` that signed it.
A Google Cloud identity: a `serviceAccountKey`, or an account to `impersonate`, with a `project`.
A cluster login: a whole `kubeconfig`, or a `token` with the `server` and its `ca`, and the `context` to use.
A login to an image or module registry: `server`, `user` and `password`.
An SSH login: `user` with a `privateKey`, a `password`, or `agent: true`; a `passphrase` for the key and a `certificate` for it.
A bearer token, with the `scheme` it is sent under.
A `user` and `password`, with a `domain` where the host needs one.

from.description: `ambient`: the tool finds the credential for itself, so no secret field is needed.

oneOf.description: The tool finds the credential for itself: its environment, its profile, its agent. The declaration names and types the identity without Meridian holding any of it.

password.description: With `ssh`, `usernamePassword` and `registry`: the password, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

privateKey.description: With `ssh`: the private key, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`. With `certificate`: the certificate's private key.

passphrase.description: With `ssh`: the passphrase of the private key, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

agent.description: With `ssh`: the key is in the SSH agent, so none is given here.

certificate.description: With `ssh`: the certificate signed for the key. With `certificate`: the certificate, in PEM form.

ca.description: With `certificate` and `kubeconfig`: the certificate authority to trust, in PEM form.

domain.description: With `usernamePassword`: the Windows domain of the user.

token.description: With `token` and `kubeconfig`: the token, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

scheme.description: With `token`: the scheme the token is sent under, such as `Bearer`.

server.description: With `registry`: the registry's host. With `kubeconfig`: the API server.

kubeconfig.description: With `kubeconfig`: the whole kubeconfig file, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

accessKeyId.description: With `aws`: the access key id, which goes with `secretAccessKey`.

secretAccessKey.description: With `aws`: the secret access key, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

sessionToken.description: With `aws`: the session token of temporary keys, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

profile.description: With `aws`: a profile of the AWS configuration to use.

clientSecret.description: With `azure`: the application's client secret, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`. A `certificate` (as `${{ secret.<name> }}`, since it holds the key) stands in for it.

managedIdentity.description: With `azure`: use the managed identity of the machine this runs on.

serviceAccountKey.description: With `gcp`: the service account's key file, as `${{ secret.<name> }}`.

impersonate.description: With `gcp`: a service account to impersonate.

Import.description: A value the document's tool is handed from another document of the workflow.

name.description: The name the value arrives under, as the tool's own variable or parameter.

oneOf.description: The text of a file another document compiles to, named by `ref` and `file`.
A value another document's apply produced, named by `ref` and `output`.

ref.description: The `metadata.name` of the document the value comes from.

file.description: With `from: artifact`: the compiled file whose text is the value.

output.description: With `from: output`: the output whose value it is.

sensitive.description: Mask the value wherever Meridian prints.

Dependency.description: A hard ordering constraint: the named resource is applied before this one.

resource.description: The id of the resource that must be applied first.

ifMissing.description: What to do when a `when` condition has removed the named resource.

oneOf.description: Refuse to compile when the named resource is not in the compiled document. This is the default.
Drop this edge when a `when` condition has removed the named resource.

when.description: A condition on this dependency alone. When it is false the entry is dropped and both resources stay.

Notification.description: A trigger: when this resource changes, the named resource performs an action.

resource.description: The id of the resource to notify.

on.description: The event that fires the notify.

oneOf.description: Fire when the notifying resource really changed. This is also what leaving `on` out means.

action.description: What the notified resource does, such as `restart` or `reload`. Which actions exist depends on the target and the notified resource's type.

ifMissing.description: What to do when a `when` condition has removed the named resource.

oneOf.description: Refuse to compile when the named resource is not in the compiled document. This is the default.
Drop this edge when a `when` condition has removed the named resource.

when.description: A condition on this notify alone. When it is false the entry is dropped and both resources stay.

id.description: The resource's name within the document. `dependsOn`, `notifies` and `${id.param}` references use it, so it must be unique.

type.description: What kind of thing the resource is. The target decides which types exist.

state.description: The state the resource should be left in, such as `present` or `running`. Each type has a default, used when this is left out.

when.description: A condition Meridian decides while compiling, from the values given with `--data`. When it is false the resource is left out of the compiled document. Example: `data.env == "prod" && defined(data.region)`.

runtimeWhen.description: A condition written in the tool's own language and checked on the node at the moment of apply. Only a target that can express it accepts it.

adopt.description: The tool's own identifier of a thing that already exists, such as `i-0abc123` for an `aws_instance`. The tool takes it under management instead of creating it. Only a target that can adopt accepts it.

params.description: The resource's settings. The target and the resource type decide which params exist.

dependsOn.description: Resources that must be applied before this one.

notifies.description: Resources to trigger when this one changes.

Output.description: A value this document hands to later documents in the workflow.

name.description: The name later documents ask for the value by.

value.description: Where the value comes from, usually a reference to something the tool reports after applying, such as `${web_vm.public_ip}`.

when.description: A condition on the output. When it is false the output is not declared.

InfrastructureSpec.description: What an Infrastructure document provisions, and what it hands on.

target.description: The target plugin that compiles this document and runs its tool, such as `ansible` or `terraform`.

targetVersion.description: The version of the target's tool to compile for. Only a target that declares versions accepts it.

when.description: A condition on the whole document. When it is false the document is skipped.

variables.description: Named values, worked out once per document and read as `var.<name>`.

conditions.description: Named conditions, read as `cond.<name>` by any `when` in the document.

secrets.description: The secrets the document reads, each a name and where it comes from, read as `secret.<name>`.

credentials.description: The identities the document names, each a name, a type and the type's fields, used by name wherever a credential is asked for, such as `targetHost.credential`.

settings.description: The tool's own settings for the whole document, such as which engine runs it or how its host is reached. Each target says which keys it takes, on its page; a key the target does not take is refused.

imports.description: Values handed to the document's tool from other documents of the workflow.

resources.description: The resources that make up the document. At least one is required.

outputs.description: Values this document hands to later documents, such as a new machine's address.

then.description: A fixed public IP address, which a vm takes with its `address` param. Reads on every target: `${id.address}`, `${id.id}`.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

network.description: The network the firewall belongs to, as a reference: `${net}`.

rules.description: The traffic allowed, one mapping per rule: `direction` (`in`, the default, or `out`), `protocol` (`tcp`, the default, `udp`, `icmp` or `any`), `port` (one port, `80`, or a range, `8000-9000`; left out for every port) and `cidr` (where the traffic comes from, or goes to; `0.0.0.0/0` for anywhere). location.description: On AWS, the availability zone the subnet is in, such as `eu-west-1a`. Refused on Azure, where a subnet is wherever its network is.

network.description: The network the subnet is in, as a reference: `${net}`.

public.description: Whether a machine in the subnet gets a public address of its own and can reach the internet. Off unless given.

then.description: A virtual machine in a subnet, from an image, of a size, reachable with a key. Reads on every target: `${id.id}`, `${id.privateAddress}`, `${id.publicAddress}`.

address.description: A fixed public address to attach, as a reference to an `address` resource: `${ip}`.

firewalls.description: The firewalls that apply to the machine, as references: `[${web_fw}]`.

image.description: What the machine boots: a mapping with `family` (`ubuntu` or `debian`) and `version` (`24.04`, `22.04`, `12`), which the target turns into the cloud's own image and shows in the compiled file; or the cloud's own image written as text, which is passed through.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

size.description: How big the machine is: a mapping with `cpus` and `memoryGb`, which the target turns into the smallest of the cloud's own sizes that has at least that and shows in the compiled file; or the cloud's own size written as text, which is passed through.

sshKey.description: The public key that may log in, as text or as a secret.

subnet.description: The subnet the machine is in, as a reference: `${web}`.

user.description: The login the key is for. Where a cloud decides the login from the image, the param is refused rather than ignored.

Resource.terraform.description: A resource of the terraform target.

then.description: A fixed public IP address, which a vm takes with its `address` param. Reads on every target: `${id.address}`, `${id.id}`.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

tags.description: Labels on the resource, as a mapping of text to text.

then.description: A set of rules saying which traffic may reach, or leave, the machines it is attached to. Reads on every target: `${id.id}`.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

network.description: The network the firewall belongs to, as a reference: `${net}`.

rules.description: The traffic allowed, one mapping per rule: `direction` (`in`, the default, or `out`), `protocol` (`tcp`, the default, `udp`, `icmp` or `any`), `port` (one port, `80`, or a range, `8000-9000`; left out for every port) and `cidr` (where the traffic comes from, or goes to; `0.0.0.0/0` for anywhere). Everything not allowed is refused. A firewall with no `out` rule lets everything out, which is every cloud's default.

port.description: One port, or a range `from-to`; every port when left out.

cidr.description: Where the traffic comes from, or goes to.

tags.description: Labels on the resource, as a mapping of text to text.

then.description: A private network with its own address range: a VPC, a virtual network. Reads on every target: `${id.id}`.

cidr.description: The network's address range, such as `10.0.0.0/16`.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

tags.description: Labels on the resource, as a mapping of text to text.

then.description: A range of addresses inside a network, where machines are placed. Reads on every target: `${id.id}`.

cidr.description: The subnet's address range, inside the network's, such as `10.0.1.0/24`.

location.description: On AWS, the availability zone the subnet is in, such as `eu-west-1a`. Refused on Azure, where a subnet is wherever its network is.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

network.description: The network the subnet is in, as a reference: `${net}`.

public.description: Whether a machine in the subnet gets a public address of its own and can reach the internet. Off unless given.

tags.description: Labels on the resource, as a mapping of text to text.

then.description: A virtual machine in a subnet, from an image, of a size, reachable with a key. Reads on every target: `${id.id}`, `${id.privateAddress}`, `${id.publicAddress}`.

address.description: A fixed public address to attach, as a reference to an `address` resource: `${ip}`.

firewalls.description: The firewalls that apply to the machine, as references: `[${web_fw}]`.

image.description: What the machine boots: a mapping with `family` (`ubuntu` or `debian`) and `version` (`24.04`, `22.04`, `12`), which the target turns into the cloud's own image and shows in the compiled file; or the cloud's own image written as text, which is passed through.

location.description: Where the resource is placed, as an Azure location such as `westeurope`. Unless given: `spec.settings.location` on Terraform, the resource group's location on Bicep. Refused on AWS, where a resource is in the region its provider is configured for.

name.description: The resource's name in the cloud. The resource's id unless given.

size.description: How big the machine is: a mapping with `cpus` and `memoryGb`, which the target turns into the smallest of the cloud's own sizes that has at least that and shows in the compiled file; or the cloud's own size written as text, which is passed through.

sshKey.description: The public key that may log in, as text or as a secret.

subnet.description: The subnet the machine is in, as a reference: `${web}`.

tags.description: Labels on the resource, as a mapping of text to text.

user.description: The login the key is for. Where a cloud decides the login from the image, the param is refused rather than ignored.
